source_excerpts.text:
Claim: any H in (T) has a finite decomposition

  H(X) = sum_l H_{B_l}(X),
  H_B(X) = {V_B,X}/2 - B X B,
  B=B*, V_B=2 Lyap_s^(-1)(B s B), Lyap_s(V)=sV+Vs.       (D)

One may take every B_l traceless, with at most (dim B)^2-1 noises. This count
is an upper bound for a finite representation, not an efficient-acquisition
claim. No representation of a reference-dependent generator is used.

Proof. The maps T_t=exp(-tH)=G^(-1)exp(-tL_*)G are CP: both G and G^(-1)
are CP congruences. They are HS self-adjoint, H preserves adjoints, and H(s)=0.
Use vec A=sum_ij A_ij |i> tensor |j> and the Choi convention
C(T)=sum_ij T(E_ij) tensor E_ij. Let e=vec I and Q project onto e-perp.
Differentiating C(T_t)>=0 at t=0 on e-perp gives

  Y = Q C(-H) Q >= 0.

Define the antiunitary J_c(vec A)=vec(A*). Direct matrix indices give
C(T^dagger)=J_c C(T) J_c for an adjoint-preserving map. Since H is HS
self-adjoint, C(-H), Q, and Y are J_c invariant. A finite positive matrix
commuting with this conjugation has an orthonormal real eigenbasis in each
eigenspace. Thus

  Y = sum_l |vec B_l><vec B_l|,

with B_l Hermitian and traceless, absorbing the nonnegative eigenvalue into
each vector. This is the Choi matrix of Phi(X)=sum_l B_l X B_l.

R_0=C(-H)-C(Phi) is Hermitian, J_c invariant and Q R_0 Q=0. Consequently
R_0=|vec A><e|+|e><vec A| with A Hermitian: write its only surviving blocks
on span(e) plus e-perp, choose the real diagonal coefficient half in each
term, and use J_c invariance for the off-diagonal vector. Under the displayed
Choi convention these two rank-one terms are A X + X A. Therefore
H(X)={V,X}/2-Phi(X), V=-2A Hermitian. Finally H(s)=0 says
Lyap_s(V)=2 sum_l B_l s B_l. The invertibility of Lyap_s for faithful s
proves (D), with V=sum_l V_{B_l}.

Each elementary term is itself physical. Set
K=d B d^(-1), D_B=d V_B d^(-1). Lyap_s(V_B)=2 B s B gives
(D_B+D_B*)/2=K* K. Hence its transported positive generator is

  L_{*,B}(X)=(D_B X+X D_B*)/2 - K X K*,

a standard Lindblad dissipator plus a Hamiltonian commutator, and it is
trace preserving and fixes sigma. Its weighted transform is HS self-adjoint.
Thus every summand is legal; not just an algebraically signed decomposition.
The CP trace-preserving semigroup implies spectrum(H_B)>=0 by similarity and
HS self-adjointness, so E_B>=0. Sums preserve this property.

2. Modular-frequency notation for one elementary noise

Work on

projections. The finite real frequency set is

  F={u_a-u_b : P_a B P_b is nonzero},
  B_alpha=sum_{u_a-u_b=alpha} P_a B P_b,
  B=sum_alpha B_alpha, B_alpha*=B_{-alpha},
  K=sum_alpha exp(alpha/2) B_alpha.                         (F)

When local s has degeneracies, P_a may have arbitrary rank; no basis inside
it is chosen and coincident frequencies are combined. The reference has no
effect on the local frequency set. A zero frequency is allowed.

Diagonalize the FULL joint state:
  rho=sum_i q_i^2 |i><i|, q_i>0,
and set
  beta_ij=log(q_i/q_j),
  c_alpha(i,j)=<i|B_alpha|j>.

For kappa real, put lambda=kappa/2 and define on ALL real x,y

  k_lambda(x)=x sinh x-lambda(cosh x-1),
  T_lambda(x,y)=x sinh y+y sinh x
                  -4lambda sinh(x/2)sinh(y/2),
  K_lambda(x,y)=T_lambda(x,y)/(2cosh((x-y)/2)).              (K)

The symbol K_lambda is a scalar kernel and is distinct from the physical
noise K in (F). It is finite at zero and at repeated/opposite points.

3. The exact complete identity

For ONE elementary Hermitian noise in any local and reference dimension,

  J_B-kappa E_B
   = 2 sum_{i,j} q_i q_j
       sum_{alpha,gamma in F} conjugate(c_alpha(i,j))
        K_{kappa/2}(beta_ij-alpha,beta_ij-gamma)
        c_gamma(i,j).                                    (G)

Both i=j and i!=j terms are included. This is an ordered-pair sum with the
factor TWO shown, not an unordered-pair sum with the same factor. Frequencies
of opposite sign and complex matrix elements must be retained. We now prove
(G), including the full physical potential, rather than postulate its sign.

3a. The stationary/root potential in frequency coordinates

Let P_sigma=-L_B(log sigma), where L_B is the Heisenberg adjoint of L_{*,B}.
Writing the physical D_B in its Hermitian plus skew-Hermitian parts shows
that the Hamiltonian trace against log rho is zero, but it generally has
a nonzero stationary-log trace. The following formula RETAINS that trace:

  P_sigma=d^(-1)[2 B s u B - {V_B,2 s u}/2]d^(-1).

For a product B_alpha* B_gamma put
m=(alpha+gamma)/2, h=(alpha-gamma)/2. If its local matrix element follows
the path b<-a->c, then alpha=u_a-u_b, gamma=u_a-u_c. Hence

  2s_a/(s_b+s_c)=exp(m)/cosh h,
  (s_b u_b+s_c u_c)/(s_b+s_c)=(u_b+u_c)/2+h tanh h.

The Lyapunov formula and the displayed P_sigma therefore give EXACTLY

  V_B=sum_{alpha,gamma} [exp(m)/cosh h] B_alpha* B_gamma,
  P_sigma=su
